root.description: false: the configuration of a package in a repository whose own configuration is above. Checked from the top, it applies to this folder (its patterns start here); checked from here, the top configuration is used, with its root and suppressions, and only this folder is checked. It cannot set plugins, include or suppressions. Default: true.

anyOf.description: A built-in preset.
A plugin preset ("namespace/name"), a package or a file.

extends.description: Presets and configurations applied before this one, in order; later ones win.

plugins.description: Packages or files whose default export is a plugin: more rules and presets.

include.description: Globs of the files looked at; like exclude, a pattern matches a file or any folder above it ("src" takes everything in src). Default: every file git knows about, or every file under the root without git.

exclude.description: Globs of files and folders left out, on top of .gitignore. A pattern without "/" matches at any depth; "!x" removes an inherited x, and brings no file back.

naming.description: How file names are read. Lists accumulate across presets; "!x" removes an inherited "x".

companions.description: Regular expressions removed from each stem, so that companion files join their module: "_test$" makes foo_test.go part of foo.go; "^test_" makes test_foo.py part of foo.py.

ignoreLeadingWords.description: Lowercase words skipped at the start of a name before reading what it is about: "i" for C# interfaces (IUserService), "bp" for Unreal blueprints (BP_Door).

groupNumericPrefixes.description: Whether names that start with a number (0001_initial, 2024-01-01-post) group by it. Default: false.

folderFiles.description: Globs of file names that describe their folder instead of being one more thing in it, and are not counted: package-info.java, __init__.py, doc.go, mod.rs.

folderCompanions.description: Endings that, after the name of a sibling folder, make a file that goes with that folder and is not counted: ".meta" makes the Scripts.meta of Unity part of Scripts/.

folderCase.description: How the folder a move proposes is written from the words of its group: "kebab" user-list (default), "snake" user_list, "camel" userList, "pascal" UserList (C# namespaces, PSR-4), "lower" userlist (Java and Go packages).

reservedWords.description: Words a folder cannot be called, because it would be a package or module name and the language reserves it (abstract in Java, async in Python, type in Go): a move proposes the plural (abstracts/), or no folder when that is reserved too. Compared with the folder name as folderCase writes it.

keepInPlace.description: Globs of paths (or of a folder above them) that a move never touches, because a tool reads them by name and place: Spring's application-*.yml, Flutter's main_*.dart, patch-package's patches. They are left out of the groups prefix-groups proposes and of what redundant-prefix renames.

routes.description: Whether a file's path is its address (Expo Router's and Next.js's app/): a group then moves into a route group, (sign)/, which does not change the address, the names are kept, and redundant-prefix does not shorten them. Default: false.

groupFileStays.description: Whether the module named exactly like a group stays beside the folder it gets: in Rust, render.rs declares the module whose files go in render/ (render_json.rs → render/json.rs). Default: false: render.ts goes into render/.

mirrors.description: Trees that mirror another one, as "source => mirror", where "**" stands for the part both share: "**/src/main/java/** => **/src/test/java/**". A problem found in both trees is reported once, in the source, and its moves take the mirrored files along.

rules.description: Rules by name, built-in or "namespace/rule" from a plugin.

max-files.description: A folder holds at most `max` files (or modules): past that it is scrolled, not read.

anyOf.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

items.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

count.description: "files" counts every file; "modules" counts a module and its companions once (`foo.ts`, `foo.spec.ts`, `foo.html` are one).

filesPerModule.description: With count "modules", a module of more files than this counts once for every this many: 25 View+X.swift extensions folded into View count as 5 with 5. Default: 0, a module counts once however many files it has.

warnAbove.description: A second, lower limit: a folder over it and within `max` is a warning, and only over `max` does it take the severity of the rule. { "max": 20, "warnAbove": 10 } fails CI at 21 and still shows the folders past 10. Default: 0, no second limit.

hint.description: Added to the message: how to split in this ecosystem, or what a new folder costs.

hintFor.description: Globs of file names: the hint is added only when the files the problem is about include one ("*.java", "*.{c,h}"). A hint about packages is noise on a folder of SQL. Default: always.

dotfiles.description: Whether files whose name starts with a dot count. Default: false — they are mostly tool settings (.gitignore, .editorconfig) that have to live where the tool looks. recommended leaves every dot-file out with ".*" in exclude, so for true to see them, exclude only the dot-folders: "exclude": ["!.*", ".*/"].

prefix-groups.description: At least `min` modules whose names start with the same word belong in a folder named after it: `render-json`, `render-text`, `render-sarif`, `render-pr` are a `render/` folder that was never made.

anyOf.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

items.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

min.description: How many modules sharing a prefix make a group.

anyOf.description: The longest prefix that keeps the group.

words.description: How many leading words form the prefix: 1 groups `user-list` with `user-card`; 2 needs `user-list-*`; "auto" takes the longest prefix that still has `min` modules and more than half of the group (`RegistroHorario*` rather than `Registro*`).

ignore.description: Prefixes that are never a group, lowercase, words joined with "-": a verb shared by unrelated files, or a convention such as `use`.

hintFor.description: Globs of file names: the hint is added only when the files the problem is about include one ("*.java", "*.{c,h}"). A hint about packages is noise on a folder of SQL. Default: always.

dropPrefix.description: Whether a move drops the prefix the new folder already says: render-json.ts goes to render/json.ts, as redundant-prefix asks. False where a file is named after the type it holds (a Java or C# class, a Unity script): renaming the file would rename the type. Default: true.

hint.description: Added to the message: what making a folder costs in this ecosystem ("In Go a folder is a package: …").

max-folders.description: A folder holds at most `max` subfolders: a long list of folders is a drawer too.

anyOf.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

items.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

max.description: How many subfolders it may hold.

redundant-prefix.description: Modules inside a folder do not repeat the folder's name: `render/render-json.ts` says render twice; `render/json.ts` says it once. A module named exactly like its folder (`render/render.ts`) is its main file and is fine.

anyOf.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

items.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

min.description: How many modules have to repeat the name before it is reported: 1 reports every one.

single-file-folders.description: A folder that holds one file and no subfolders is a level of nesting with nothing to group: keep the file in its parent until it has company. The other side of `max-files`, for those who split too early.

anyOf.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

items.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

allowed.description: Globs of files that may be alone in their folder because something outside requires it: `main.go` of a Go command, `lib.rs` of a crate. Matched like `exclude`: a pattern without "/" is a file name at any depth, one with "/" is a path from the root.

case-collision.description: Two files or folders of one folder whose names differ only in case or in Unicode normalisation (`Components/` and `components/`, `Foo.ts` and `foo.ts`, `café` written two ways) are one name on Windows and macOS: git cannot check both out there, and one silently overwrites the other.

anyOf.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

items.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

scattered-feature.description: A feature is one folder, not a word repeated in every layer folder: `RegistroController`, `RegistroService`, `RegistroRepository`, `RegistroDto` and `Registro` in `controller/`, `service/`, `repository/`, `dto/` and `model/` are a `registro/` package nobody made. Reported once, at the folder that holds the layers, with every move.

anyOf.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

items.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

layers.description: Names of the folders that hold a layer, in any case, singular or plural: `service` matches `service/`, `services/` and `Services/`.

min.description: In how many layer folders of one folder a word has to start a name to be reported.

ignore.description: Words that start names in every layer and are no feature, lowercase: `base`, `api`, `app`.

hint.description: Added to the message: what a feature folder is in this ecosystem.

orphan-companions.description: A file an engine keeps next to an asset (Unity's `Player.cs.meta`, Godot's `icon.png.import` and `player.gd.uid`) has its asset beside it. One without it is what is left when the asset was moved, renamed or deleted outside the editor, or committed without it: the ID it held is gone, and every reference to the asset breaks.

anyOf.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

items.description: "error" fails the run, "warn" reports without failing, "off" does not run the rule.

suffixes.description: The endings of the files that go with an asset, each a dot and a word: `X.meta` goes with the file or folder `X`. "!.uid" takes one out.

emptyFolders.description: Whether to report a companion of a folder that is not there (`Glade.meta` with no `Glade/`). Git stores no empty folder, so an empty folder's `.meta` is committed alone, and Unity makes the folder again when it sees it. Default: false. A companion of a name without an extension is taken for a folder's.

type-folders.description: A folder is named after what its assets are for, not what type they are: `Rocks/` holds the mesh, textures and materials of the rocks, where `Textures/`, `Materials/` and `Meshes/` spread one rock over three folders. For game engines, whose editors already filter by type.

overrides.description: Settings for some folders only. Every override says why.

folders.description: Globs matched against folder paths relative to the root; the root itself is ".".

withFiles.description: Globs of file names: the override applies only to the folders that hold one of them directly ("package.json" is the root of a package). Default: every folder matching "folders".

extends.description: Presets applied to these folders only, before the settings of the override: ["java"] under "server/**". reason.description: Why these folders are different, in at least 10 characters once trimmed. Required: an override is a silence, and a silence without a reason cannot be reviewed.

expires.description: A date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC) after which the override is reported as config/expired-override, a warning: it still applies, and says it is due for review.

owner.description: Who answers for it (a person or a team, such as @org/team): shown with it.

ticket.description: Where the work that removes it is tracked (an issue number or a link): shown with it.
